successors.name: State of Rabih az-Zubayr
successors.text: 'In 1893, Kanem-Bornu was conquered by the Sudanese warlord Rabih az-Zubayr'; Rabih made Dikwa his capital

capitals.name: Njimi (site not located on the page)

ledger.x: c. 1070s: Kanem under the Sayfawa, 'with a core territory in the region of Kanem (northeast of Lake Chad)'. 'In the 11th century, the empire converted to Islam and the Duguwa were replaced with the Sayfawa dynasty'; 'overthrown in the second half of the 11th century by mai Hummay'. The page dates the empire's…
c. 1250: Kanem rules the Fezzan. 'In the mid-13th century, Kanem ruled the Fezzan as far as Waddan.' The Dunama page: 'control the entire Fezzan region'. The page names no previous ruler.
ledger.cp: Fezzan rulers (no state named by the page)

ledger.x: Within Dunama's reign (approximately 1221-1259): the Bornu region comes under firm Kanem control.
ledger.cp: Sao and other peoples of the Bornu region (the page names the Sao)

ledger.x: Mid-14th century: the Fezzan slips away.
ledger.cp: Fezzan rulers (no state named by the page)

ledger.x: c. 1380: the Bilala drive the mai from Kanem. 'Around the year 1380, the Bilala were able to oust the Sayfawa from power in Kanem.' 'Imperial control of the lands east of Lake Chad was terminated'; the Bornu land west of the lake stays with the mai.
c. 1380: Njimi is abandoned and the empire moves to Bornu. 'Njimi... abandoned after c. 1380'; 'After the fall of Njimi, the empire lacked a permanent capital for about a century.'
c. 1472: Mai Ali founds Ngazargamu. 'In c. 1472, Ali founded the empire's first substantial capital city, Ngazargamu.'
Early 1500s: Idris III Katagarmabe retakes Kanem.
Under Idris Alooma (reign 'approximately 1570-1603') the Bilala of Kanem are fought again.
The Kanem frontier is settled by treaty: 'a peace agreement was reached with Abdullah, the Bilala mai of Kanem', with 'clear demarcations to define the borders'.
1808: the Fulani take Ngazargamu.
1809: the south-western borderlands go to the Fulani.
1814: Muhammad al-Kanemi builds Kukawa.
1824: Bornu defeats Bagirmi and occupies the Kotoko cities.
ledger.cp: Kotoko city states of Kousseri, Ngulfai and Logone (no dossier; Bagirmi, defeated in the same year, is a belligerent of the war entry)

ledger.x: Later in the 1820s: the Fulani are driven out of Bornu.
1846: the al-Kanemi shehus replace the Sayfawa mais.
May 1893: Rabih az-Zubayr invades Bornu.
February/March 1894: Rabih beats Kyari on the Yobe.
1894: Bornu passes to Rabih.
1894: the Kanem-Bornu Empire ends as an independent state.

wars.name: Bilala conquest of Kanem and the Bornu recovery
wars.outcome: The Bilala ousted the Sayfawa from Kanem around 1380; the mais ruled from Bornu and Idris III Katagarmabe reconquered Kanem in the early 1500s.

wars.name: Idris Alooma's Kanem expeditions
wars.outcome: More than five expeditions into Kanem ended in a peace with the Bilala mai Abdullah and a demarcated border (undated).

wars.name: Fulani jihad against Bornu
wars.outcome: The Fulani destroyed Ngazargamu in 1808 and held the south-western districts; Muhammad al-Kanemi saved the mai and 'later in the 1820s' drove the Fulani out of Bornu proper.

wars.name: Bornu-Bagirmi war
wars.outcome: Al-Kanemi defeated Bagirmi in 1824 and occupied Kousseri, Ngulfai and Logone.

wars.name: Rabih's conquest of Bornu
wars.outcome: Rabih took Kukawa in 1893 (Amja, May 1893; Lekarawa about August) and beat Kyari at Dimurwa on the Yobe in February/March 1894; Bornu became his military dictatorship.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a frontier of Kanem or Bornu; the Sahel and Lake Chad margins are approximate.
